steps.say: Slip percentage stages the disease. Meyerding turns a bending X-ray into a grade that decides brace versus screws.
steps.tx: **Meyerding grades** (slip percent scale) stage slip as percent displacement from **I below 25** (one, quarter slip) to **V above 100 percent** (five, full drop) **spondyloptosis** (fallen vertebra), and instability means significant slip progression or more than **3 to 4 mm** (three to four millimetres) motion on **flexion-extension films** (bend X-rays).

vis.alt: Lumbosacral slip with Scotty dog pars defect, Meyerding grading scale and compressed root.
vis.caption: Spondylolisthesis slip with Scotty dog defect and Meyerding scale. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Young athletes crack the bridge while older women slide the joint. The collar on the X-ray dog separates them.
steps.tx: **Isthmic lysis** (bridge crack slip) from **pars defects** (bridge breaks) shows the **Scotty dog collar** (neck break sign) on oblique views in young athletes, while **degenerative slip** (worn joint slide) at L4-L5 with intact arch and stenosis affects elderly women with back and leg pain.

steps.say: Low stable slips heal without steel. Bracing and muscle work carry most grade one disease.
steps.tx: Low-grade stable slips without stenosis are managed conservatively with **bracing** (belt support) and **core strengthening** (trunk muscle work), and **pars repair** (bridge fixing) suits adolescents while fusion suits adults with pain or slip risk on standing films, with extension-based programs avoided in active slips.

steps.say: Fusion has a short honest list. Instability, deformity, destroyed joints and proven painful motion qualify, nothing else.
steps.tx: **Fusion** (bone joining operation) is indicated for instability, high-grade slip, recurrent prolapse with **facetectomy** (joint removal), deformity and chronic axial pain with proven instability, not for uncomplicated first prolapse or pure leg pain without back pain, with leg-dominant pain still starting non-operatively, as **fusion indications** (joining reasons) stay narrow.

vis.alt: Lumbar spine pain generators including disc, facet, stenosis, slip and muscle strain.
vis.caption: Lumbar pain generators from disc to slip and stenosis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Approach names describe the corridor. Back, front and side routes each trade muscle damage against cage size.
steps.tx: **TLIF** (back-side cage operation) gives unilateral transforaminal access with one cage, **PLIF** (back both-side operation) gives bilateral access with more retraction, **ALIF** (front cage operation) gives the largest **lordotic cage** (curve restoring block) anteriorly, and XLIF spares back muscles through the psoas.

steps.say: Bone heals poorly in smokers and the sugar-uncontrolled. Optimise the host before booking the steel.
steps.tx: Smoking, diabetes and **osteoporosis** (thin bone illness) raise **pseudoarthrosis** (failed joining) risk, so **smoking cessation** (quit smoking), glycaemic control and bone health optimisation precede elective fusion, with **BMP** (bone growth protein) reserved for high-risk cases and revisions, plus vitamin D repletion as part of bone optimisation.

steps.say: Stiff segments load their neighbours. A small yearly wear rate needs mentioning before consent.
steps.tx: **Adjacent segment disease** (neighbour wear illness) follows rigid fusion at about **2 to 3 percent** (two to three percent) per year, counselled preoperatively alongside dural tear, infection and **hardware failure** (metal breakage) as the standard complication set, with smoking doubling the neighbour-wear rate.

steps.say: Teenage high slips with tight hamstrings never brace alone. Reduction and screws protect the nerves and the future.
steps.tx: High-grade **dysplastic slips** (birth defect slides) in adolescents with L5 radiculopathy and **hamstring tightness** (back thigh stiffness) need **reduction fusion** (straighten and join) with screws, never bracing alone, with L5 root monitoring through the reduction manoeuvre and growth-friendly constructs in the very young.
